items.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Well I went with Jimmy Dorsey and I played, I had two guitars.

ctx.x: Tell us a little about that story you told us you were going to tell us about the Dorsey band.

Oh, yeah. Well I went with Jimmy Dorsey and I played, I had two guitars. I had a rhythm guitar and an electric guitar. So there was a guitar feature in the band and I knew about it. So I got the record before I joined him and I learned it. And it was sort of difficult. It was a chord solo with a few single notes and it was the melody, so you had to play it pretty close to the way it was written you know. And I was a very bad reader in those days. And so we were on the job the first night and Jimmy gave me a…
So then did you have to back it up from that point on?

items.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Well we were all three with Jimmy Dorsey.

ctx.x: Tell me a little bit about how the Soft Winds Trio came together.

Well we were all three with Jimmy Dorsey. And I think the bassist Johnny Frigo, I think got us, that we could play in a certain room, I think it was in Detroit. So we loved Jimmy Dorsey’s orchestra and Jimmy Dorsey. So we drew straws to see who had to tell him we were leaving. And Johnny Frigo, the bassist lost. He had to tell him. And Jimmy was very upset needless to say. And the guitar book, I had a lot of ensemble with the horns written. And some of it was pretty difficult. So Jimmy just negated that and got a…
I see. It’d be hard to replace that kind of player.
